outages.place: Paraná, including Foz do Iguaçu, Londrina, Cascavel, Maringá, and other cities
outages.cause: Storms and two F1 tornadoes that damaged the electrical system with strong wind gusts, lightning, and fallen trees, according to Copel, with Simepar confirming the tornadoes
outages.affected: Copel, as reported by CGN in an article published at 6:47 p.m. Brasília time Saturday, Nov 21 (3:47 p.m. CT), and by Folha de Curitiba in an article published at 12:05 a.m. Brasília time Sunday, Nov 22 (9:05 p.m. CT Saturday), said that 54,246 consumer units remained without power in Paraná as of 6:30 p.m. Brasília time Saturday (3:30 p.m. CT), and that 299,603 units, or 85 percent of the customers affected by Friday's storms, had already been reconnected, with about 1,000 professionals in the field. Those reports, citing Copel, said the remaining outages at that bulletin were concentrated in the West (15,600 units), North (14,600), Northwest (10,800), Southwest (6,700), Centro-Sul and Campos Gerais (3,300), and Curitiba, the metropolitan region, and the coast (2,900). Among the cities with the most customers still out were Foz do Iguaçu (4,200), Londrina (2,800), Cascavel (2,700), Guaraqueçaba (2,000), Lapa (1,800), Apucarana (1,600), and Maringá (1,200). Copel also said a new storm on Saturday afternoon affected the East and part of the South, with the most customers then out in Guaraqueçaba (2,000), Lapa (1,800), Matinhos (445), and Paranaguá (390). Simepar confirmed two F1 tornadoes on Friday, Nov 20, one around 3:00 p.m. Brasília time (noon CT Friday) in the Vila Yolanda neighborhood of Foz do Iguaçu and another around 6:00 p.m. Brasília time (3:00 p.m. CT Friday) in Manoel Ribas, with estimated winds of 117 to 180 km/h. An earlier Copel bulletin issued at noon Saturday, as reported by Tribuna do Interior at 2:40 p.m. Brasília time Saturday (11:40 a.m. CT), said 80,588 units remained without power at that earlier hour, 273,261 had been restored (77.2 percent), and the peak had been 353,849 units at 8:02 p.m. Brasília time Friday (5:02 p.m. CT Friday). G1, in a Jornal Nacional report published at 10:10 p.m. Brasília time Saturday (7:10 p.m. CT), said more than 50,000 houses in Paraná were still without power after the two tornadoes, and likewise reported that more than 350,000 properties had lost power on Friday night. No later official Copel remaining-outage count after the 6:30 p.m. Saturday figure of 54,246 consumer units was found as of 6:00 AM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (9:00 a.m. Brasília time Sunday). No official firm restoration time for all remaining customers was given; Copel said work would continue until supply was restored to all affected customers.
outages.start: Afternoon and evening of Friday, Nov 20, 2026 (Brasília time), when storms and two F1 tornadoes hit Paraná; the peak of 353,849 consumer units was recorded at 8:02 p.m. Brasília time Friday (5:02 p.m. CT Friday), according to Copel's Saturday noon bulletin as reported by Tribuna do Interior

outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, including a large-scale overnight and morning attack on Nov 20 and further strikes reported on Nov 21 and into Nov 22
outages.affected: Ukraine's Energy Ministry, in a Facebook statement reported by Ukrinform at 11:05 a.m. EET Sunday, Nov 22 (3:05 a.m. CT), by SNN.UA at 10:13 a.m. EET Sunday (2:13 a.m. CT), and by RBC-Ukraine in an article dated 1:30 p.m. EET Sunday (5:30 a.m. CT), said that during the previous day Russia had again attacked a number of energy facilities, and that as of Sunday morning some consumers were without electricity in the Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Rivne, Odesa, and Kharkiv regions, with energy workers working to restore supply. The ministry said the most difficult situation as of Sunday morning remained in Odesa region, where repeated attacks had substantially complicated restoration work and a large number of consumers remained without electricity. It said that on Sunday morning energy workers had managed to begin partially restoring power to critical-infrastructure facilities in Odesa and surrounding areas, that ensuring their stable operation remained the first priority, and that specialists were also working on backup supply schemes and other technical solutions to gradually restore electricity to remaining consumers. The ministry said the damage was extensive, so repairs would take time. Vitalii Bunechko, head of the Zhytomyr regional military administration, as reported by Ukrinform at 10:05 a.m. EET Sunday (2:05 a.m. CT), said that over the previous day Russian forces had carried out four drone strikes on energy facilities in Zhytomyr region. No official customer count was given for Zhytomyr or for the five regions as a group. Ukrenergo, as reported by UA.NEWS at 9:23 a.m. EET Sunday, Nov 22 (1:23 a.m. CT), and earlier Saturday evening by LB.ua at 10:42 p.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (2:42 p.m. CT), by 24tv in an article updated at 10:14 p.m. EET Saturday (2:14 p.m. CT), by OBOZ.UA at 9:59 p.m. EET Saturday (1:59 p.m. CT), by Focus at 10:59 p.m. EET Saturday (2:59 p.m. CT), by UNN at 8:20 p.m. EET Saturday (12:20 p.m. CT), and by RBC-Ukraine at 11:05 p.m. EET Saturday (3:05 p.m. CT), said that on Sunday, Nov 22, planned electricity outages would be in effect around the clock in parts of the country: hourly outage schedules of 1 to 2.5 groups, or queues, for all categories of consumers, and capacity-restriction schedules for industry. Those reports, citing Ukrenergo, said the restrictions were the result of Russian attacks on the power system, that the electricity-supply situation remained difficult in Odesa and Rivne regions, where emergency restoration work was continuing, and that consumers should check current schedules on the official pages of their distribution-system operators. No official nationwide customer count was given in those Sunday-schedule announcements. No official nationwide customer count, and no official change cancelling those Sunday all-day schedules, was found as of 6:00 AM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (2:00 p.m. EET Sunday).
outages.updated: Nov 22, 2026, Energy Ministry Sunday morning update on outages in Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Rivne, Odesa, and Kharkiv regions, with the most difficult situation remaining in Odesa region and partial restoration of critical infrastructure beginning Sunday morning in Odesa and surrounding areas, via Ukrinform 11:05 a.m. EET Sunday (= 3:05 a.m. CT), SNN.UA 10:13 a.m. EET Sunday (= 2:13 a.m. CT), and RBC-Ukraine 1:30 p.m. EET Sunday (= 5:30 a.m. CT); Zhytomyr OVA head Vitalii Bunechko via Ukrinform 10:05 a.m. EET Sunday (= 2:05 a.m. CT) on four drone strikes on energy facilities in the previous day; Ukrenergo Sunday all-day schedules of 1 to 2.5 queues still in effect, via UA.NEWS 9:23 a.m. EET Sunday (= 1:23 a.m. CT) and Saturday evening reports via LB.ua, 24tv, OBOZ.UA, Focus, UNN, and RBC-Ukraine; rechecked 6:00 AM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (2:00 p.m. EET Sunday), no official nationwide customer count and no official cancellation of those Sunday schedules found

outages.place: Odesa and parts of Odesa district
outages.cause: Repeated Russian attacks on high-voltage transmission networks and other energy facilities critical to the region, including a strike on a DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi energy facility on the morning of Nov 20. Ukraine's Energy Ministry said that as of Sunday morning, Nov 22, the situation in Odesa region remained the most difficult, that repeated attacks had substantially complicated restoration work, and that a large number of consumers remained without electricity
outages.affected: Ukraine's Energy Ministry, in a Facebook statement reported by Ukrinform at 11:05 a.m. EET Sunday, Nov 22 (3:05 a.m. CT), by SNN.UA at 10:13 a.m. EET Sunday (2:13 a.m. CT), and by RBC-Ukraine in an article dated 1:30 p.m. EET Sunday (5:30 a.m. CT), said that as of Sunday morning the most difficult situation remained in Odesa region. The ministry said repeated attacks had substantially complicated restoration work, that a large number of consumers remained without electricity, and that on Sunday morning energy workers had managed to begin partially restoring power to critical-infrastructure facilities in Odesa and surrounding areas, with ensuring their stable operation the first priority. It said specialists were also working on backup supply schemes and other technical solutions to gradually restore electricity to remaining consumers, and that the damage was extensive, so repairs would take time. No official Sunday morning customer count was given. Ukrenergo, as reported by UA.NEWS at 9:23 a.m. EET Sunday (1:23 a.m. CT) and earlier Saturday evening by LB.ua at 10:42 p.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (2:42 p.m. CT), by 24tv in an article updated at 10:14 p.m. EET Saturday (2:14 p.m. CT), and by Focus at 10:59 p.m. EET Saturday (2:59 p.m. CT), said the electricity-supply situation remained difficult in Odesa region, where emergency restoration work was continuing. DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi, in an official article dated Nov 21 and posted on its website, said that according to the Energy Ministry, as of the evening of Nov 21 the situation in Odesa region remained difficult, that strikes on high-voltage, or main, transmission networks were triggering automatic protection systems, and that large-scale outages were occurring in part of Odesa district, including Odesa. Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa regional military administration, as reported by Ukrinform and by RBC-Ukraine at 7:30 p.m. EET Saturday (11:30 a.m. CT), said electricity supplies in the region remained unstable and that power outages had been occurring throughout Saturday in parts of Odesa district, including the city of Odesa, because of attacks on high-voltage transmission networks; he also said disruptions to heating and water supplies remain possible. No official Saturday evening or Sunday morning customer count was given in the ministry, regional-administration, DTEK, or Sunday-schedule statements. Earlier Friday, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi, in an official Nov 20 evening statement, said 8,000 families in 21 settlements remained without power after the morning attack, and that crews would work overnight to restore power to another 15,600 families in 55 villages and towns after weather-damage cleanup; earlier Friday morning, 41,000 households were without power in the Odesa and Rozdilna districts, according to DTEK's press service as reported by Ukrainska Pravda and Ekonomichna Pravda. No official Saturday evening or later remaining-customer count was found as of 6:00 AM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (2:00 p.m. EET Sunday).
outages.updated: Nov 22, 2026, Energy Ministry Sunday morning statement that Odesa region remained the most difficult, that a large number of consumers were still without electricity, that partial restoration of critical infrastructure in Odesa and surrounding areas had begun Sunday morning, and that repairs would take time, via Ukrinform 11:05 a.m. EET Sunday (= 3:05 a.m. CT), SNN.UA 10:13 a.m. EET Sunday (= 2:13 a.m. CT), and RBC-Ukraine 1:30 p.m. EET Sunday (= 5:30 a.m. CT); Ukrenergo via UA.NEWS 9:23 a.m. EET Sunday (= 1:23 a.m. CT) and Saturday evening reports via LB.ua, 24tv, and Focus on the situation remaining difficult, with emergency restoration work continuing; Saturday evening Energy Ministry, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi, and Oleh Kiper statements; earlier Friday official DTEK remaining 8,000 families after the morning attack and earlier Friday morning 41,000-household figure; rechecked 6:00 AM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (2:00 p.m. EET Sunday), no official Saturday evening or later remaining-customer count found

outages.cause: Russian attacks that seriously damaged energy equipment in Sarny district. Rivneoblenergo has said hourly outage schedules did not apply in the affected communities because these were emergency outages from the damage
outages.affected: The Rivne regional military administration, as reported by Rayon.in.ua at 10:25 a.m. EET Sunday, Nov 22 (2:25 a.m. CT), said that about 50 settlements in the Sarny area of Rivne region were still without electricity because of damage to energy infrastructure from Russian attacks. The report said Rivneoblenergo crews, who had worked the previous day, were continuing repairs on Sunday, and that restoration was being complicated by significant damage to energy facilities and by frequent air-raid alerts, so power could not yet be restored promptly to all of the settlements. No official Sunday customer count was given. Ukrenergo, as reported by UA.NEWS at 9:23 a.m. EET Sunday (1:23 a.m. CT) and earlier Saturday evening by LB.ua at 10:42 p.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (2:42 p.m. CT) and by 24tv in an article updated at 10:14 p.m. EET Saturday (2:14 p.m. CT), said the electricity-supply situation remained difficult in Rivne region, where emergency restoration work was continuing. Rivnepost, at 11:00 p.m. EET Saturday (3:00 p.m. CT), reported Sunday hourly schedules in Rivne region and said emergency outages were still ongoing in certain communities where those schedules do not apply; that report did not give a new official Sarny remaining-settlement count. Rivneoblenergo, as reported by Rivne Media at 9:05 p.m. EET Saturday (1:05 p.m. CT), said drone strikes the previous day and that day had damaged a large number of energy facilities in the Sarny area, with restoration work to continue Sunday, and did not give a new official remaining-settlement count. Earlier Saturday, Rivneoblenergo, as reported by Rivne Vechirnie (Rivnepost) at 11:35 a.m. EET Saturday (3:35 a.m. CT) and by Rivnenski Novyny at 10:22 a.m. EET Saturday (2:22 a.m. CT), said 46 settlements in Sarny district were still without power and that these were emergency rather than scheduled outages. Oleksandr Koval, head of the Rivne regional military administration, as reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 1:04 a.m. EET Saturday (5:04 p.m. CT Friday), had said 50 settlements were without power. No later official remaining-settlement or customer count, and no official firm restoration time, was found as of 6:00 AM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (2:00 p.m. EET Sunday).

outages.place: Kurdistan Region, including Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Duhok, Bazian, and Chamchamal
outages.cause: Suspected drone attack on the Khor Mor gas field on the night of Nov 8, 2026, which halted gas production that supplies much of the region's electricity generation. Dana Gas, the field's operator, later said the facility had sustained significant damage and could produce no gas
outages.affected: Al Jazeera, on Nov 9, 2026, citing Iraqi and Kurdish officials, said a Sunday-night drone attack on the Khor Mor gas field caused a fire and left more than 70 percent of the Kurdish region without power. Omid Ahmed (also spelled Omed Ahmed), spokesperson for the Kurdistan Regional Government's Ministry of Electricity, said the attack suspended gas supply to power plants in Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Bazian, Chamchamal, and Duhok, and knocked between 2,500 and 2,800 megawatts of generation off the grid, Al Jazeera reported, citing the official Iraqi News Agency (INA). Rudaw later quoted Ahmed as saying that authorities had increased generation from approximately 1,000 megawatts immediately after the attack to 1,550 megawatts, of which 50 megawatts were reserved for essential facilities and factories, leaving 1,500 megawatts for residents and raising daily public electricity supply to six to eight hours, reaching nine hours in some areas. Ahmed said the electricity then available covered only 40 percent of the region's demand, leaving a 60 percent shortfall, and that no date had been established for production to resume. Rudaw's article image assets for that report are dated Nov 13, 2026. Dana Gas, in a Saturday statement reported by Rudaw, said the facility had sustained significant damage and that currently no amount of gas could be produced. 964media, in a Nov 15 report, quoted Ahmed as saying that no timeframe had been set for electricity supplies to return to normal and that the ministry was waiting for gas from Khor Mor to flow again; in that interview he also said that within 48 hours of the attack the ministry had increased generation from 1,000 megawatts to nearly 1,650 megawatts, and that some areas were then getting more than eight hours of grid power a day, particularly on holidays. The same report said grid supply had fallen to three to four hours a day right after the attack and was later raised to six to seven hours, and that Dana Gas had said the field could produce no gas. The Insight International, in a Nov 21 report citing private-generator council officials who spoke to Rudaw on Saturday, Nov 21, said the public grid remained weak because of the gas shortfall after the Khor Mor attack, and that neighborhood generators were still running for most of the day. It quoted Khoran Khorani, head of Erbil's supreme council of private generator owners, as saying that 80 to 90 percent of Erbil's generators were providing 14 hours a day, and Osman Mohammed, head of the association of private generator owners in Sulaimani, as saying generators in central Sulaimani were running 13 hours a day and had started running on Nov 10. Hakar Harori, head of the council of private generator owners in Duhok, said generators in and around the city were running from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m. and again from 1 p.m. to 1 a.m. No official customer count was given. No later official ministry generation figure, and no official confirmation that Khor Mor production had resumed, was found as of 6:00 AM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (2:00 p.m. Iraq time Sunday).
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. As of the latest official statements found, no date had been established for Khor Mor production to resume.
outages.updated: Nov 8–21, 2026 attack and aftermath: Al Jazeera Nov 9 citing Iraqi and Kurdish officials and INA; KRG electricity ministry figures via Rudaw (article image assets dated Nov 13); Dana Gas still-shut statement via Rudaw and 964media; Omed Ahmed via 964media Nov 15 on no timeframe for a return to normal supply and on generation rising to nearly 1,650 megawatts within 48 hours of the attack; The Insight International Nov 21, citing private-generator officials who spoke to Rudaw on Saturday, Nov 21, on the public-grid shortfall continuing and on private generators still running about 13 to 14 hours a day in Erbil and Sulaimani; rechecked 6:00 AM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (2:00 p.m. Iraq time Sunday), no later official generation figure or confirmation that Khor Mor production had resumed found

outages.place: Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Yenakiieve, Debaltseve, Torez, Snizhne, and nearby districts
outages.cause: A massive attack on energy infrastructure on the night of Nov 22, 2026, according to occupation government head Andrei Chertkov, who said new outages were added to the effects of earlier damage; earlier official accounts had also described local accidents, a power deficit, and network overloads
outages.affected: Occupation government head Andrei Chertkov, as reported by Kommersant at 11:34 a.m. Sunday, Nov 22 (2:34 a.m. CT if Moscow time), by NEWS.ru at 11:25 a.m. Sunday (2:25 a.m. CT if Moscow time), by Moscow 24 at 11:14 a.m. Sunday (2:14 a.m. CT if Moscow time), and by Vedomosti in a Nov 22 article, said that after a massive overnight attack on energy facilities, electricity supply had been disrupted across a large part of the occupied Donetsk region and that more than 279,000 subscribers remained without electricity. Those reports, citing Chertkov, said that as of Sunday morning, Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Yenakiieve, Debaltseve, Torez, and Snizhne were partially without power, and that outages were also reported in settlements in the Volnovakha, Amvrosiivka, Telmanove, Yasynuvata, and Volodarske municipal districts, a total of 12 municipalities. Chertkov said the new outages were added to the effects of earlier damage, that energy workers had come under attack but that none of them was injured, and that repair crews had already begun work despite the threat of further attacks. No official firm restoration time was given. Earlier Sunday morning, occupation city head Aleksey Kulemzin, as reported by Lenta.ru at 9:20 a.m. Sunday, updated at 9:27 a.m. Sunday (12:20 a.m. and 12:27 a.m. CT if Moscow time), and by Vesti at 8:22 a.m. Sunday (11:22 p.m. CT Saturday if Moscow time), said that all districts of Donetsk were partially without power. Those reports, citing Kulemzin and Donetskenergo, said 347 transformer substations had disconnected automatically, leaving 36,655 subscribers without electricity, and that, because permissible network load had been exceeded, 58 transformer substations had also been disconnected, leaving 4,700 subscribers without electricity; Vesti stated that more than 40,000 subscribers were without electricity in the city. NEWS.ru, in its Sunday report on the later Chertkov figures, also said that on Nov 21 energy workers had restored power to all Donetsk subscribers who had been left without electricity by network overloads and emergency disconnections on the evening of Nov 20. An earlier Saturday morning official region-wide remaining total of more than 107,000 subscribers as of 7:00 a.m. Saturday, reported by the occupation ministry via DNR News at 10:12 a.m. Saturday (1:12 a.m. CT if Moscow time), citing Donetskenergo, was superseded by the Sunday morning Chertkov figure of more than 279,000 subscribers. No later official region-wide remaining total after that Sunday morning figure of more than 279,000 subscribers was found as of 6:00 AM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (3:00 p.m. Moscow time Sunday).
outages.start: Night of Sunday, Nov 22, 2026, local time, for the attack described by occupation officials; other partial outages in the region were already being reported
outages.updated: Nov 22, 2026, occupation government head Andrei Chertkov via Kommersant 11:34 a.m. Sunday (= 2:34 a.m. CT if Moscow time), NEWS.ru 11:25 a.m. Sunday (= 2:25 a.m. CT if Moscow time), Moscow 24 11:14 a.m. Sunday (= 2:14 a.m. CT if Moscow time), and Vedomosti, on more than 279,000 subscribers remaining without power as of Sunday morning after an overnight attack, with Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Yenakiieve, Debaltseve, Torez, Snizhne, and nearby districts partially unpowered; earlier Sunday morning occupation city head Aleksey Kulemzin via Lenta.ru 9:20 a.m. Sunday, updated 9:27 a.m. Sunday (= 12:20 a.m. and 12:27 a.m. CT if Moscow time), and Vesti 8:22 a.m. Sunday (= 11:22 p.m. CT Saturday if Moscow time), on 36,655 subscribers plus 4,700 more in Donetsk city; NEWS.ru note that the Friday evening Donetsk city accident had been restored on Nov 21; earlier Saturday morning official region-wide total of more than 107,000 subscribers as of 7:00 a.m. Saturday, superseded by the Sunday Chertkov figure; rechecked 6:00 AM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (3:00 p.m. Moscow time Sunday), no later official region-wide remaining total after the Sunday morning figure of more than 279,000 subscribers found

outages.place: Crimea and Sevastopol, including Yevpatoria, Dzhankoy, Bilohirsk, and other districts
outages.cause: A power-capacity shortage after strikes on transmission networks outside the peninsula, according to occupation sources. Krymenergo said consumption-restriction measures continued on Sunday, Nov 22, because of insufficient incoming electricity, and Sevastopolenergo said a temporary restriction regime was in effect on dispatcher orders
outages.affected: Krymenergo, as reported by RIA Novosti Crimea at 9:11 a.m. Sunday, Nov 22, updated at 9:13 a.m. Sunday (12:11 a.m. and 12:13 a.m. CT if Moscow time), said consumption-restriction measures remained in effect in Crimea on Sunday because of insufficient incoming electricity, that outage schedules could not be observed under the circumstances, and that information on the introduction of restrictions would be published separately. In a later report at 1:30 p.m. Sunday (4:30 a.m. CT if Moscow time), RIA Novosti Crimea, citing Krymenergo, said electricity supply had been restricted in parts of Yevpatoria and of the Bakhchysarai, Bilohirsk, Kirovske, Razdolne, and Simferopol districts. That report listed, among other places, Syren and, in what it called the Sevastopol district, Verkhnesadove, Pirohovka, and Frontove; the Bilohirsk-district villages of Nyzhni Orishnyky, Verkhni Orishnyky, Balanove, Kurortne, and Krasnohiria; Razdolne-district settlements including Slovianske, Avrora, Kotovske, Sterehushche, Ohni, Kukurushkino, Nyva, Ryleievka, and Slavne; Zolote Pole, Vidrodzhennia, Pryvitne, and part of Abrykosivka in Kirovske district; and, partly, Krasnolissia, Mramorne, and Dobry in Simferopol district. Krymenergo said the planned time for restoring supply was three hours, and that supply in Yevpatoria had also been restricted on a list of streets, also for about three hours. The same report said earlier Sunday accounts had described the Yalta area as without power because of network accidents, and restrictions in Dzhankoy and surrounding villages, in Kirovske district, and in Feodosiya. An earlier Krymenergo list, reported by RIA Novosti Crimea at 9:36 a.m. Sunday and updated at 9:58 a.m. Sunday (12:36 a.m. and 12:58 a.m. CT if Moscow time), named streets and lanes in Dzhankoy, villages in Dzhankoy district, places in Bilohirsk, Bakhchysarai, Razdolne, and Kirovske districts, part of Pervomaiske, and streets in Yevpatoria, and likewise said the outages were expected to last about three hours. Sevastopolenergo, as reported by RIA Novosti Crimea at 9:45 a.m. Sunday (12:45 a.m. CT if Moscow time), said a temporary electricity-restriction regime had been introduced on the orders of the dispatcher, following a 3-hours-on, 3-hours-off rotation: until noon, groups 3 and 4 would have power and the others would be partly disconnected; from noon to 3:00 p.m., groups 1 and 2; from 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m., groups 3 and 4; from 6:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m., groups 1 and 2; and from 9:00 p.m. to midnight, groups 3 and 4 again. The company said the energy-system situation in Crimea remained unstable and that the dispatcher could introduce additional restrictions if needed. Occupation sources have said peninsula-wide interruptions began Oct 24, 2026, after strikes on transmission networks outside the peninsula. No official customer count was given. No official notice that the general deficit-related restrictions had been lifted was found as of 6:00 AM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (3:00 p.m. Moscow time Sunday).

outages.cause: Generation-capacity deficit in the national electric system. UNE's Saturday bulletin said unit 8 of CTE Mariel, units 1 and 2 of CTE Santa Cruz, and unit 2 of CTE Felton were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, unit 1 of CTE Felton, and unit 5 of CTE Renté were in maintenance, with thermal-generation limitations of 394 MW
outages.affected: CiberCuba, in a page updated at 6:14 a.m. Cuba time Sunday, Nov 22 (5:14 a.m. CT), citing reports from electric companies, said that on Sunday there were local deficit-related outages in Havana, Holguín, and Sancti Spíritus. It said Havana reported 86 circuits affected and 207 MW at 3:32 a.m. Cuba time Sunday (2:32 a.m. CT), that Holguín reported a 106 MW deficit at 6:00 a.m. Cuba time Sunday (5:00 a.m. CT), and that national available generation was 1,039 MW at 6:00 a.m. Cuba time Sunday. CiberCuba said no total collapse of the national grid was recorded. It also presented those Sunday morning figures as reports from the utilities, not as an official UNE daily bulletin, and continued to display UNE's Saturday forecast as the latest official forecast, not Sunday's figures. No official UNE Sunday bulletin, and no official Saturday evening-peak actual from UNE, was found as of 6:00 AM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (7:00 a.m. Cuba time Sunday). UNE's Saturday bulletin, published by Cubadebate on Saturday, Nov 21, and also reported by Juventud Rebelde, which posted the same official figures at 8:36 a.m. Cuba time Saturday (7:36 a.m. CT) and updated the article at 8:54 a.m. Cuba time Saturday (7:54 a.m. CT), said the national electric system continued to face a generation-capacity deficit. It said service had been affected by a capacity deficit throughout all 24 hours on Friday, Nov 20, and that the affectation continued through the early morning, with a maximum affectation of 1,799 MW recorded at 7:10 p.m. Cuba time Friday (6:10 p.m. CT Friday). It said solar-photovoltaic parks produced 4,177 MWh, with a maximum of 650 MW delivered in the midday period. At 6:00 a.m. Cuba time Saturday, Nov 21 (5:00 a.m. CT), the bulletin said SEN availability was 980 MW against demand of 2,270 MW, with 1,295 MW affected. For the midday period it estimated an affectation of 1,400 MW. For the evening peak, UNE estimated that unit 8 of CTE Mariel would enter with 45 MW, and it forecast availability of 1,025 MW against a maximum demand of 2,800 MW, a deficit of 1,775 MW, and, if those conditions held, an affectation of 1,805 MW at the peak. Official UNE sources did not report a total collapse of the national grid.

outages.cause: Fuel shortages affecting electricity generation, according to the state electricity company Tavanir
outages.affected: Planned electricity restrictions began in Iran on Sunday, Nov 22, 2026, according to the state electricity company Tavanir. RFE/RL, in a report dated midnight CET Sunday, Nov 22 (5:00 p.m. CT Saturday), said the cuts started Nov 22 and quoted Tavanir chief executive Mohammad Allahdad as telling state television that the outages are expected to last up to two hours a day depending on location. The same report quoted Allahdad as saying on Nov 21 that, given the country's fuel-supply conditions, the electricity sector would be forced to impose distribution restrictions from Sunday. Nour News, in a report dated 8:09 a.m. Iran time Sunday, Nov 22, or 1 Azar 1405 (10:39 p.m. CT Saturday), and Eghtesad Online, in a report dated 8:29 a.m. Iran time Sunday (10:59 p.m. CT Saturday) that cited Nour News, said planned electricity restrictions began today, the first of Azar, and attributed that announcement to the chief executive of Tavanir. Those reports said the restrictions were being imposed because of special fuel-supply conditions and the need to manage consumption, in order to help keep the power network stable. They said, citing the Tavanir chief executive, that the new restrictions may take the form of a two-hour outage over two days, or a maximum of two hours each day, and that the timing is not fixed and may change with network conditions. They said customers would be informed of outage times through the Bargh-e Man system and app, the Bale messenger app, and text messages. Tavanir had announced on Saturday, Nov 21, that planned electricity restrictions on households and businesses would begin on Sunday, Nov 22, because fuel shortages were disrupting power generation, according to Iran International in a report dated 5:11 p.m. GMT Saturday, Nov 21 (11:11 a.m. CT), and to RFE/RL. Iran International, citing Tavanir, quoted Allahdad as saying that outages could last up to two hours every two days, and could increase to two hours daily as temperatures fall, and that the country's gas production remained below last year's levels. Anar News, in a report updated at 12:05 a.m. UTC Sunday, Nov 22 (6:05 p.m. CT Saturday), citing BBC Persian, also said planned power outages began in Iran on Sunday, Nov 22, because of fuel shortages at power plants. No official customer count was given in those reports. No official nationwide remaining-customer count was found as of 6:00 AM CT Sunday, Nov 22 (2:30 p.m. Iran time Sunday).

outages.cause: Drone attacks on power stations and other electricity infrastructure during the war between the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces
outages.affected: No official customer count. Drop Site News, in a Nov 20, 2026 report from Khartoum, said a particularly intense wave of drone strikes at the end of October and into November targeting power stations, fuel supplies, and electricity infrastructure had brought the country's power grid to the brink of collapse, and that two weeks after the wave of attacks, major substations remained out of service. Shaker Ismail, an engineer with the Sudanese Electricity Company, told Drop Site that repairing some of the country's most important power facilities could take months or longer, that high-capacity transformers and digital control systems had been damaged, and that replacement transformers must be manufactured to order abroad. Ismail said the Um Dabakir thermal power plant in White Nile State was badly damaged in an Oct 29 strike and forced to shut down, and that the Al-Markhiyat substation west of Omdurman was put out of service after an Oct 27 strike; he said affected areas continued to experience prolonged outages and scheduled power cuts as of this week. The report said the Sudan Electricity Holding Company and Ministry of Energy had yet to publicly announce the restoration of the major facilities damaged in the attacks. A United Nations report published Nov 17, issued in Geneva and posted on the UN in Sudan website, said that in just over two weeks between Oct 20 and Nov 4, 29 drone strikes, attributed to the Rapid Support Forces, hit electricity facilities and fuel stations across 11 states, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines. An earlier Al Jazeera Nov 15 feature said there is no clear schedule for the resulting power cuts, which can last anywhere between six hours and a day, and, citing The Associated Press, said repeated drone attacks on power stations have seen electricity generation fall from about 4,400 megawatts before the war to about 1,100 MW. Residents and a small-business owner in Port Sudan described prolonged, unreliable cuts, including outages lasting more than 24 hours. No later official national customer count or restoration timetable was found as of 6:00 AM CT Sunday, Nov 22.
